canonical_name: Max-flow min-cut theorem family for finite capacitated networks
literal_source_claim_zh: 网络流的最大值等于最小割容量
literal_source_claim_en: The maximum value of a network flow equals the minimum cut capacity.
source_attribution: L. R. Ford / D. R. Fulkerson, 1956
candidate_claim_not_credited_as_statemen: For a finite capacitated network with source and sink, the greatest value of a feasible source-to-sink flow equals the least capacity of a source-sink cut; the graph model, capacity codomain, flow representation, cut definition, extrema, binders, and boundary cases are not frozen.
statement_blocker: The catalog gives only an equality gloss. The inspected 1956 theorem uses a finite undirected graph, positive numeric arc capacities, and nonnegative weighted simple source-to-sink chain flows, whereas a modern formal target may use directed edge flows and conservation. Selecting either encoding, or silently allowing zero capacities and different cut conventions, would invent proposition-changing details before source review and checked transport.
domain_and_universes: Open: the source-selected target must fix a finite graph or multigraph model, vertex and edge universes, source and sink, capacity codomain, flow representation, cut representation, and all required finiteness and decidability instances.
conclusion: Open as an exact expression: equality between the source-approved maximum feasible flow value and minimum source-sink cut capacity, including attainment if the selected formulation asserts maxima and minima.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake. The statement phase must resolve every case listed in scope-map.md.
